task: Every quarter I compare the MD&A to last year's and flag what changed.
I tie out every number in the 10-Q draft back to the trial balance and the footnote schedules.
Posting accrual and reclass journal entries in the ERP during the first five days of close.
I chase the business unit controllers for their flux explanations. Every month it's the same three people who are late.
Final sign-off on the earnings release before it goes to the audit committee chair.
Uploading the filing package to EDGAR and checking the accepted status plus the XBRL rendering.
I roll forward last quarter's footnotes and update the numbers, then send them to the auditors for review.
Deciding whether a variance is big enough to need disclosure in the MD&A. Mostly judgment, honestly.
Build the board deck every quarter: pull the actuals, update the charts, write the commentary on the key drivers.
Reconciling intercompany balances across 14 entities and booking the eliminations.
chasing legal for the litigation update every quarter so we can finalize the contingencies footnote
I read through the peer companies' 10-Ks to see how they worded their new revenue disclosures.
Running the FX remeasurement and posting the resulting entries before consolidation.
Reviewing the tax provision memo and signing off on the effective rate before we lock the numbers.
Updating the forecast model each month with new headcount and revenue assumptions, then writing the variance commentary for the CFO.
I send reminder emails to all the account owners about close deadlines and keep a tracker of who's submitted their reconciliations.
Drafting the risk factors update. I compare against the prior filing and see what's new in the business.
Proofreading the whole 10-K for typos and inconsistent numbers, which takes me about two weeks of evenings.
Approving manual journal entries over the threshold. I look at support and decide whether it's right.
One-off: we're implementing the new lease standard and I'm building the schedules and drafting the disclosures.
Scheduling the disclosure committee meetings and collecting everyone's section sign-offs beforehand.
I summarize the auditor's comments and make a list of what needs to be fixed in the next draft.
Cross-checking the numbers in the earnings script against the press release and the tables.
Preparing the segment reporting tables and checking they foot and cross-foot to the consolidated statements.
Calculating the share-based comp expense and EPS dilution each quarter, then booking the entries.
Waiting on department heads for their budget submissions. I send nudge after nudge during planning season.
Writing the CFO's talking points for the earnings call and anticipating analyst questions.
Tagging the financial statements in XBRL and fixing validation errors before filing.
Deciding how to account for an unusual acquisition. I read the guidance, write the memo and get the controller's approval.
Month-end I pull the bank and subledger balances and compare them to GL, investigating anything that doesn't match.
I test a sample of 25 access reviews each quarter and document whether the evidence supports the control.
Chasing control owners for evidence. Honestly it's 60% of my job, sending the same email three times.
Updating the RCM every year, comparing the old control descriptions to what the process owners say is happening now.
Signing off on the SOX control test results and deciding whether a deficiency is significant or just a deficiency.
Uploading screenshots and reports into the audit folder and naming them per our convention.
Drafting audit findings: I read the testing workpapers and write up the condition, cause, effect and recommendation.
Reviewing policies once a year to see if they still match regulations and what we actually do.
I maintain the risk register, scoring new risks and rescoring old ones after the quarterly risk meeting.
Mapping our controls to ISO 27001, SOC 2 and NIST so we don't test the same thing twice.
Scheduling walkthroughs with process owners and sending out the meeting invites and PBC lists.
Final approval on the internal audit report before it goes to the audit committee.
One-time project: moving our controls out of spreadsheets into one system and cleaning up duplicates.
I read vendor SOC 2 reports and note exceptions plus whether our complementary user entity controls cover them.
Following up with IT on remediation of open findings, and updating the status tracker weekly.
Reviewing the population from the system and picking samples for testing, then recalculating the numbers for the sample.
Writing the audit plan for next year based on risk assessment and talking it through with the CAE.
I compare the control narratives to the flowcharts and look for mismatches.
Certifying quarterly: I make the sub-certification requests, track who's responded, and escalate no-shows.
Evaluating whether compensating controls are enough when a segregation-of-duties conflict comes up. Pure judgment call.
Summarizing long policy docs and regulations into plain bullet points for the business teams.
Pulling user access lists from the ERP and checking terminated employees were removed on time.
Preparing the PBC list for the external auditors and handing over evidence as it comes in.
Reviewing management's remediation plans and deciding if the fix is adequate to close the issue.
I do the risk assessments for new vendors: read their questionnaire answers and rate them.
Tracking when each control is due for testing and sending reminders to owners and testers.
Updating the framework mapping after a regulation changes, e.g. matching new requirements to existing controls.
Approving exceptions to policy when someone asks. I weigh the risk and write down why.
Checking that the evidence uploaded actually covers the right period and the right system. A lot of it doesn't.
Running the annual fraud risk assessment workshop and writing up the output.
Reconciling the deficiency log to the issues in the audit tool so the numbers reported to the committee match.
Every year I rewrite the climate section of our sustainability report so the narrative matches the new emissions data.
I chase site managers for their monthly electricity and gas meter readings. Half of them reply only after the third reminder.
Calculating Scope 1 emissions from fuel purchases using the latest DEFRA emission factors, then reconciling totals against last year.
I sign off the double materiality assessment conclusions before they go to the board. Mostly deciding which topics clear the threshold.
Sending the CDP questionnaire out to the team leads, and then nagging them till every answer is in.
reading through supplier survey responses and summarizing them into one table for Scope 3 category 1, its tedious but needs doing
Prepping evidence folders for the limited assurance audit: pulling invoices, calculation sheets and policy docs, labeling each against the ESRS datapoint.
Mapping our existing disclosures to ESRS datapoints to find gaps. One-off project this year, though we'll need to update it annually.
Uploading the final emissions numbers to the CDP portal and checking that each response saved correctly.
Reviewing drafts from the climate and water chapter owners and leaving comments where the numbers don't match the data tables.
I run the stakeholder interviews for double materiality, then write up the impact and financial materiality scoring with the reasoning behind each score.
Scope 2 location-based and market-based calcs. I update the grid factors and supplier-specific factors and check the spreadsheet formulas.
Approving the final wording of our transition plan disclosure after legal has had their say.
Emailing 200 suppliers the annual sustainability questionnaire and tracking who has opened it, who replied, and who is ignoring me.
Translating ISSB S2 climate-related risk requirements into questions for our risk team, then summarizing their answers for the report.
Answering the assurance provider's follow-up questions about how we got the waste data. Usually means digging through old emails.
building the Scope 3 business travel number from the travel agency export, cleaning flights vs rail and applying factors
Deciding with the CFO which Scope 3 categories are material enough to report this year. Judgment call, with a lot of back and forth.
Keeping the sustainability data glossary and methodology notes up to date so they match what we actually did in the calcs.
I collect water withdrawal figures from factories. Some send PDFs, some Excel, some just a number in an email.
Year-end: write the sustainability statement text for each ESRS standard, reusing last year's wording and updating figures and targets.
Checking that numbers in the narrative equal the numbers in the tables, line by line, before it goes to assurance.
Scheduling the quarterly data collection calendar with all sites and sending the reminders on the right dates.
Review of the GHG inventory boundary: deciding which acquired sites and leased assets are in or out under operational control.
Gathering HR numbers for the social metrics: headcount, turnover, training hours, safety incidents. Different HR systems per country so it's messy.
One-time project: setting up our first CSRD report. Figuring out the scope, the owners, and the timeline.
Responding to customer ESG questionnaires, mostly copying answers from our report and checking they're still current.
Converting units and currencies in the energy data submissions, kWh vs MWh vs GJ, so everything lines up before calculation.
Reading new regulatory guidance, like EFRAG implementation notes, and writing a short summary for the team on what changes for us.
I approve the target-setting language for SBTi alignment before it's published. Need to be sure we can back every claim.
Tracking down missing refrigerant leak records from facility managers. They never log them on time.
Drafting the executive summary and highlights page of the sustainability report once all the chapters are in.
Reconciling the year over year change in emissions and writing the variance explanations for the auditors.
Uploading the XBRL-tagged sustainability statement and checking the tags are correct before filing.
Taking the meeting notes for our monthly steering group and sending out the action list afterwards.
Weekly status update for my manager: pulling what's done, what's stuck, and writing it up in a few paragraphs.
Reviewing colleagues' drafts and leaving comments on the wording, numbers and formatting.
Keeping track of which version of the board pack is the latest. People keep saving copies with 'final_v3_REAL' in the name.
Onboarding new team members: showing them where files live, how our reporting calendar works and who to ask for what.
Answering questions from the external auditors about our year-end figures and where support documents are stored.

signing off the quarterly report after checking with finance that all figures are final
Chasing department heads for their input to the annual report. Deadlines pass and I send polite reminders again.
Proofreading the 10-K draft for typos, inconsistent terms and cross references that are broken.
Scheduling review meetings and sending calendar invites to everyone involved in the reporting cycle.
Summarizing long email threads and meeting recordings for people who missed them.
Tying out numbers between the financial statements and the notes, so that totals match everywhere.
Deciding which comments from reviewers to accept and which to push back on, then making the final call on wording.
Preparing the board paper each quarter by copying last quarter's structure and swapping in the latest results.
Setting up permissions so the right people can edit their sections and others can only view.
Collecting sign-off emails from approvers and filing them as evidence for the audit.
Writing step by step instructions for how our reporting process works, because only I know it right now.
Updating the budget vs actual commentary every quarter. Read variances, write a sentence for each big one.

Filing the completed reports with the regulator through their web portal and saving the confirmation.
Comparing the new draft against last year's version to spot what changed and make sure changes are intentional.
Reminding the team of the deadlines, and checking the tracker to see which sections are still open.
Approving expense and cost data in the reporting pack, mostly deciding whether odd-looking items need an explanation.
Formatting tables and charts in the annual report so fonts, number formats and styles are consistent.
